author: Ash

copy.intro: You've got a Comfrt hoodie in your cart, then you read the returns page: exchange or store credit, never a refund. Or you just want that roomy, heavy-fleece feel from a brand you already shop. These are the hoodie brands most often named as Comfrt alternatives, ordered by how often they come up. Each one comes with the hoodie to start with, how the fit and fabric compare, and what its returns look like.

bodies.nike:
Nike is the easiest swap if you want a loose, roomy hoodie at close to what Comfrt actually charges. Start with the Solo Fleece Pullover Hoodie ($75), a brushed cotton-polyester fleece cut in what Nike calls a loose fit.

Look at the size run first. It goes from XS to 4XL, and most sizes also come in Tall, so it's the pick on this list if you're tall. Tech Fleece is its pricier line, and the Tech Fleece Pullover Hoodie ($145) is the one to know there. Returns are where Nike pulls ahead of Comfrt: 60 days, and free for members.

Solo Fleece is midweight, though, so if it's Comfrt's heavy fleece you're after, Champion's Reverse Weave is closer.
bodies.skims:
SKIMS is the one to look at if you want plush fleece that comes with matching lounge pieces, not gym gear. The Cotton Fleece Hoodie ($98) is 70% cotton, with a small embossed logo on the left sleeve and not much else going on.

Sizes run XXS to 4X, the widest range here, so it's a good call if Comfrt's 3X stops short for you. Most of its hoodies sit at $98, and the Sweater Knit Cable Zip Up Hoodie ($128) is there if you'd like a knit instead of fleece.

Returns run 30 days, like Comfrt's. But SKIMS offers a refund too, which Comfrt doesn't, and that matters if you're unsure of the size. If $98 is more than you want to spend, Champion's Powerblend hoodies cost well under half that.
bodies.alo-yoga:
Alo is the pick for a hoodie that works from Pilates to lunch, if you're happy to pay for it. The cheapest full-price option is the Marl Sweater Rewind Full Zip Hoodie ($168), a chunky, midweight cotton blend with a relaxed, waist-grazing cut.

Most of Alo's hoodies sit in the sale, so full price means knits and cashmere, up to $398 for the Wool Cashmere New Class Full Zip Hoodie. Check the sale section before anything else. Shipping is free on every US order, and so are returns within 30 days.

It's the most expensive pick here by a distance. Sizes also stop at 2XL, so if you need more room, SKIMS and Cozy Earth both go bigger.
bodies.champion:
Champion is the budget answer, and the Reverse Weave Hoodie Sweatshirt ($70) is the closest it gets to Comfrt's heavy, slouchy shape: heavyweight fleece, a loose fit and dropped shoulders.

The fabric names tell you what you're buying. Reverse Weave is the heavy one, cut on the cross-grain so it holds its shape and shrinks less. Powerblend is the midweight line, and it's much cheaper, with styles like the Powerblend Hoodie, C Logo ($37.50). So if you want weight, pay the extra for Reverse Weave.

Delivery is the weak spot. Champion only ships to the 48 contiguous states, and you pay for return shipping. If you're torn between two sizes, Nike's 60-day window is the friendlier bet.
bodies.quince:
Quince is the cheapest way into a cashmere hoodie on this list. The Mongolian Cashmere Full-Zip Hoodie is $119.90, about a third of what Alo charges for its cashmere zip.

For something nearer to Comfrt money, start with the Flowknit Full-Zip Hoodie ($44.90). It sells factory-direct with no middlemen, and low prices are its whole pitch. The 365-day return window is the longest here by far, so there's very little risk in trying a size, and shipping is free with no minimum. Sizes run XS to XL, with 1X to 3X on some styles, so check the hoodie you want before counting on a plus size.

Its hoodie range is small and mostly zip-ups. If you want a pullover, Uniqlo and Nike both sell one.
bodies.uniqlo:
Uniqlo is the low-cost way to get Comfrt's roomy cut. Its Sweat Oversized Pullover Hoodie ($49.90) is oversized by design, as the name says, and there's a Sweat Oversized Full-Zip Hoodie ($59.90) if you prefer a zip. At under $50, it's the cheapest pullover here after Champion's Powerblend.

Both are listed in men's sizing, from XXS all the way to 3XL. So if you normally buy women's sizes, check the size chart before you order. Returns run 30 days. Shipping is free from $99, which two pullovers just clear.

Choice is limited to two styles, so if you want options, Champion has far more hoodies to pick from at similar prices.
bodies.cozy-earth:
Cozy Earth is the pick if softness matters more to you than weight. Its Brushed Bamboo Hoodie ($98) is a relaxed bamboo-viscose hoodie with a weave that Cozy Earth says lasts longer and doesn't pill.

There are women's and men's versions, and the women's Brushed Bamboo goes up to XXXL. For men, the StretchTech Hoodie ($138) is a stretchy double-knit with a three-piece hood. And like Comfrt, Cozy Earth sells bedding alongside the loungewear, so you can shop both in one order.

Returns run 30 days, and the money goes back to whatever card or account you paid with. If it's that heavy fleece you're really after, though, Champion's Reverse Weave is closer.
bodies.american-giant:
American Giant is the made-in-the-USA pick. The one to look at is the Men's Classic Full Zip ($168), a zip hoodie in sizes S to XXL, with 3X in black.

For women, the Women's Thermal Hoodie ($98) is the cheapest full-price option, in XS to XL. US shipping is free over $150, so one Classic Full Zip covers it on its own. Returns run 30 days for anything unworn and unwashed.

But it's a different kind of purchase from Comfrt. The Classic Full Zip costs more than double what any Comfrt hoodie sells for, so it suits buying one zip-up to keep, not three colors. If that's too steep, Champion's Reverse Weave is $70.

best_for.quince: a cashmere zip hoodie for about $120

best_for.cozy-earth: soft bamboo loungewear you can return for a refund
best_for.american-giant: one American-made zip hoodie instead of three cheaper ones

closing.heading: How to choose
closing.body: Start with your budget. Uniqlo's hoodies and Champion's Powerblend and Reverse Weave lines keep you at $70 or less, and Reverse Weave is the heavyweight one. Between $75 and $140, Nike suits tall frames, SKIMS goes up to a 4X, and Cozy Earth swaps fleece for bamboo. Above that, it's about what you want to own: American Giant for a hoodie made in the USA, or Quince and Alo for cashmere, with Quince at about a third of Alo's price. And if Comfrt's store-credit-only returns are what put you off, Quince gives you 365 days and Nike gives you 60.

faqs.q: How long does Comfrt take to ship?
faqs.a: Comfrt aims to process weekday orders placed before 11am PT within 24 hours. Standard US delivery then takes 3 to 6 business days, or 2 with Express ($15.95).
